instructions:
Plan one episode for the scriptwriter. Use the client's brief for the audience, genre, speaker roles and scope, and the dossier for the reporting.

## Choose what to tell

Answer the question in the brief. If the brief gives only a topic, decide what this audience would want to know about it. When several angles fit, follow each as far as its ending. Choose an opening that makes the listener want to know what happens or why, and an ending the reporting supports.

## Outline the episode

Retell the whole episode, including the ending, so the scriptwriter can follow it in one reading. Introduce people and situations as they become relevant. Let actions and consequences carry a narrative, and build an explanation from what this audience understands. Select what will actually be heard in the allotted time. A detail can give a moment life or make a number meaningful. Give each speaker a part in telling the story.

You choose material and order. Do not add your own bans on how the writer may stage or tell the story. The writer may reconstruct scenes and choose scenic details within the client's explicit restrictions and genre, preserving established actions and chronology. Invented scenic details can enliven the telling. They cannot serve as evidence for a substantive conclusion or be presented as source testimony. The writer composes the spoken lines.

Where the selected wording or sequence creates a false impression, adjust the causal link, timing, attribution or verb. If precise wording makes the account clear and accurate, stop there. Leave out objections to claims the account neither makes nor implies, whether phrased as a contrast or as a host's duty to qualify every finding. Retain conditions and uncertainty that change a selected claim's meaning. Add a separate clarification only where understanding still depends on it. Apply this throughout the plan, including speaker functions and timing notes. Write the resulting events or explanation.

## Delivery

Use `output_language` and the requested structure. Preserve supplied speaker identifiers, source quotations and catalog references exactly.
Aim for the target duration within the bounds. Count the opening, transitions and ending once.
Use `ready` without blockers and `needs_research` for a blocking evidence gap. Explain research needs. Use `plan=null` if no episode is supported. Optional material and research requests may be empty.

main_question.title: Main Question
main_question.description: Central question of the episode for this audience; the opening may raise the same question or a local one.

listener_promise.title: Listener Promise
listener_promise.description: What following the chosen story offers this audience.

working_answer.description: The chosen answer to the episode's question, with the context needed to understand it.
working_answer.title: Working Answer

route_summary.description: The chosen story from opening to ending: what happens or becomes clear, how its developments connect, and where they lead.
route_summary.title: Route Summary

title.title: Title
title.description: A short name for this part of the chosen story.

listener_question.title: Listener Question
listener_question.description: What listeners want to find out at this point in the story.

intended_change_in_understanding.title: Intended Change In Understanding
intended_change_in_understanding.description: What happens, is discovered, or becomes clear in this part.

prerequisite_concepts.title: Prerequisite Concepts
prerequisite_concepts.description: Technical knowledge needed to follow this part; an empty list is valid.

material_refs.description: Exact supplied locators supporting this act's reasoning.
material_refs.title: Material Refs

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: The timing basis for the duration estimate, such as pace, pauses, and how the parts are counted.

optional_material.title: Optional Material
optional_material.description: Specific story material that can be added or removed to fit the duration; an empty list is valid.

answer_to_deliver.title: Answer To Deliver
answer_to_deliver.description: The answer reached at the ending.

speaker_id.description: Exact speaker label from the assignment.
speaker_id.title: Speaker Id

contribution.title: Contribution
contribution.description: What this person tells, explains, notices, asks, or contributes to this particular story.

interaction_guidance.title: Interaction Guidance
interaction_guidance.description: How this narrator carries the account forward, or how the speakers' contributions build on each other.

speech_register.title: Speech Register
speech_register.description: How this person speaks for this audience and genre.

approach.title: Approach
approach.description: What listeners encounter at the start, what they learn or notice next, and how this opens the chosen story.

material_refs.description: Exact locators offered in the supplied material catalog.
material_refs.title: Material Refs

question_to_open.title: Question To Open
question_to_open.description: The question raised for listeners by this opening.

affected_act_ids.description: Local act labels; empty for an episode-wide question.
affected_act_ids.title: Affected Act Ids

material_refs.description: Relevant supplied locators; may be empty for missing evidence.
material_refs.title: Material Refs

blocking.description: Whether the promised answer requires this unresolved material.
blocking.title: Blocking

from_previous.title: From Previous
from_previous.description: How the preceding development leads into this part.

toward_next.title: Toward Next
toward_next.description: How this part leads to the next development or question.

plan.description: Complete proposal, or null when material cannot support one.
